forecasting competition.simple: An open contest where many teams forecast the same hidden data and are ranked by an agreed metric.

OWA.simple: Overall weighted average used in M4: the average of the sMAPE ratio and the MASE ratio against the Naive2 benchmark. Below 1 beats the benchmark.
OWA.example: OWA 0.82 means about 18% better than Naive2.

Prophet.simple: An open-source forecasting tool from Facebook (Meta). It adds a trend, seasonality and holiday effects.
Prophet.example: Forecast daily visits with weekly and yearly seasons.

changepoint.simple: A time where the slope of a trend is allowed to change.
changepoint.example: Growth slows down after a product matures.

Fourier series.simple: A sum of sine and cosine waves that can describe a repeating pattern.
Fourier series.example: Weekly seasonality with 3 sine and cosine pairs.

DeepAR.simple: An Amazon model: one recurrent neural network trained on many related series that outputs a probability distribution for each future step.

negative binomial.simple: A probability distribution for counts (0, 1, 2, ...) that can have more spread than a Poisson.
negative binomial.example: Daily unit sales of a product.

GluonTS.simple: Amazon's open-source toolkit for probabilistic time-series forecasting.

tokenizer.simple: A step that turns raw input into small integer codes (tokens) that a language model can read.
tokenizer.example: Chronos scales values and puts them in bins.

zero-shot.simple: Using a pretrained model on a new series without any training on that series.
zero-shot.example: Forecast a new store with Chronos without fitting.

foundation model.simple: A large model pretrained on a lot of varied data that can be used for many tasks.

TimesFM.simple: Google's time-series foundation model. It reads patches of values with a decoder-only transformer and forecasts without training on your series.
TimesFM.example: Zero-shot forecast of a Wikipedia page-view series.

patch.simple: A group of consecutive values (for example 32) that a model treats as one input unit.
